questions.answer: Projects must be git repositories (FAQ: every project must be a git repository). A folder without git can run as a session workspace instead, which has no project, branch or PR link.

questions.question: Local git without remote
questions.answer: FAQ says remotes other than GitHub work locally; a repo with no remote at all is not addressed.

questions.question: Hosted git
questions.answer: GitHub is fully supported through gh; other hosts work locally and cross-machine project identity is tied to GitHub; GitLab support is only a tracking issue.

limitations: Local projects need Git and an installed agent.

questions.question: Api
questions.answer: HTTP MCP is documented, and the early-alpha SDK exposes configurable API/relay base URLs. A stable independent REST endpoint contract remains unestablished.

questions.question: Sdk
questions.answer: Early-alpha @superset_sh/sdk supports task/workspace/project/host/agent/terminal/automation operations; docs say not production-ready and may be removed.

questions.answer: HTTP MCP at api.superset.sh/mcp exposes the current named task, workspace, agent, terminal, page, automation, host and project tools. No fixed tool count is claimed; v1 returns410.

questions.answer: Automations accept inbound POST webhook triggers using a sset_wh_ token, with no filters or de-duplication. The SDK reference does not mention webhooks. Outbound webhook delivery from Paradev is not documented.

questions.question: Operations
questions.answer: MCP/CLI cover task CRUD, workspace create/update/delete, agent launch, terminal read/send, automations and Pages; SDK covers a subset.

questions.answer: OAuth 2.1 scoped to the active organization for interactive MCP, and sk_live_ API keys (full organization access) for CLI, SDK and CI.

questions.answer: The SDK is explicitly early alpha and not for production. Current CLI docs carry no Beta label; legacy v1 MCP is removed with410, while the documented v2 path remains supported.

limitations: SDK is early alpha and explicitly not meant for production; current CLI docs do not label CLI Beta.
No installed API/CLI or authenticated MCP scenario ran.

claims.answer: Current Paradev plugins supply MCP tools and skills with agent-specific support and a vendor credential proxy. The chat /mcp command separately lists configured servers; broader MCP manager/community marketplace remain roadmap items.

questions.answer: Built-in chat /mcp lists configured MCP servers from .mastracode/mcp.json, .amp/settings.json or .mcp.json with name, transport and state. questions.question: Plugins
questions.answer: Install service plugins in the sidebar. Claude/Codex get MCP+skills; Kimi/Vibe/Grok get skills only. User config entries win over managed copies.

questions.question: Custom tools
questions.answer: Custom plugins can proxy an existing Streamable HTTP MCP server and ship skills/scripts; the tool server itself must be operated separately.

questions.question: Instructions import
questions.answer: Plugin skills and built-in skills are installed into standard agent discovery paths; user-authored copies are not overwritten.

questions.question: Authentication
questions.answer: Account-requiring plugins connect through Paradev; local configs point at its proxy and do not contain OAuth tokens.

questions.question: Permission scope
questions.answer: Slack agent plugin tools cannot delete resources, merge pull requests or perform bulk writes.

questions.question: Integration owner
questions.answer: Paradev manages plugin installation, config entries and credential proxy; the external MCP server owns its tools. Organization repositories are synced by an owner/admin.

limitations: No plugin call or credential boundary test.
MCP manager/community marketplace roadmap scope is broader than the released service-plugin catalog.

sources.title: The Superset Model
sources.locator: Projects; Workspaces; Terminals; Devices
sources.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. A workspace is an isolated git worktree on its own branch. A workspace lives on the machine that hosts its files, terminals and ports, which need not be the machine you are using. Remote access reaches workspaces hosted on another device. Automations dispatch scheduled agent runs to whichever device you pick. Sessions survive restarts. sources.locator: Creation and Branches; Status Indicators; Archiving; Deleting

sources.finding: The application's cloud engineering guide explicitly describes the sandbox VM, memory limits and swap configuration. The shipped backend provisions and resumes those environments through @vercel/sandbox. This concerns managed Cloud workspaces, not local worktree security.
